verified_claims: Kelly & Chen, Research in Business and Economics Journal vol. 14 (local text aabri.txt): betting unders on posted totals of 47.5 or more won 59.7% in 2001-09 (95-141, p=0.014 against 0.524). The rule lost in 2010-18 (under record 218 of 463 = 47.1%). They restate Paul & Weinbach's 58.7% and credit the change to how sportsbooks price. Every number matches the report.

Paul & Weinbach (2002), J. Sports Econ. 3(3):256-263, 1979-2000 (Crossref abstract): a fair bet cannot be rejected overall, but betting unders on totals 5-7 points above the mean breaks the fair-bet condition, and no-profitability is rejected at the highest totals. This matches the report, and the report's 5-points-above-season-mean replication is the right analogue.

Borghesi (2008), Applied Financial Economics 18(12):947-953, 1984-2004 (OpenAlex abstract): heat, wind and rain reduce scoring, bettors underestimate the effect, and an out-of-sample weather strategy wins significantly above 52.38%. Matches.
Kain & Logan, J. Sports Econ. 15(1):45-63 (Crossref abstract, NFL/NBA/NCAA 2004-2010): the betting line predicts margin accurately, but the over/under predicts the sum of scores poorly. Matches.

Moskowitz, 'Asset Pricing and Sports Betting', Journal of Finance 76(6):3153-3209, 2021 (DOI 10.1111/jofi.13082; PDF text checked): over/under returns are uncorrelated with spread and moneyline returns; about half of the open-to-close move is reversed at game outcome; momentum and value magnitudes fail to overcome transaction costs.

Baker & McHale (2013), IJF 29(1):122-130 (DOI verified): a point-process model with scoring hazards driven by past team stats and/or the spread and over/under. The market slightly beats it on results; it does at least as well as the market on exact scores. Matches the abstract.
Koopman & Lit, JRSS-A 178(1):167-186, and Karlis & Ntzoufras, IMA J. Management Math 20(2): both exist and both are soccer-only.
Shank (2019), IJSF 14(1):3-12 exists. The report correctly calls it unverified; its abstract is about bettor wager shares and contrarian strategies, not totals mispricing.
Open-Meteo docs: Historical Forecast API coverage 'starts around 2022'; the Previous Runs API starts January 2024 for most models.

martineastwood/penaltyblog: MIT license, active (last push 2026-09-13). It has Poisson, bivariate Poisson and Dixon-Coles models, and backtest.py builds its lookback with df[date < current date]. Verified from the source.

Every data number reproduced exactly from the report's own scripts (tot.py, joint.py, rel.py on gl.csv and tw.json): total RMSE 13.72/13.31/13.12; total R² 0.078/0.083/0.080; total slope 0.90/0.97/0.99; spread R² 0.176/0.173/0.203; open vs close total RMSE 13.38 vs 13.13 (n=1356); move slope 1.14 with SE 0.16; high-total unders 53.3% (n=383); wind of 15+ mph unders 56.6% (n=617, z=2.07; 57.7% in 2000-12, 54.9% in 2013-26); home-away residual correlation 0.021/0.002/0.035; top total 51 at 3.85% vs margin of 3 at 14.55%; the reliability table (red-zone split-half 0.04, EPA/play 0.59, PROE 0.73, and so on; n=320, 2016-2025).
The stored red-zone feature really is per play: server/services/nfl-features.js:62 defines red_zone_td_rate as 'Touchdown rate on red zone plays'.

F17 does report that Moyer et al. (2024)'s independent multi-event Poisson baseline puts roughly half the true mass on margin 3 (7.67% vs 14.7%). At margin 7 it is closer to two-thirds (5.67% vs 8.89%), so 'about half' holds only loosely.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Koopman & Lit (2015) is a 'score-driven bivariate Poisson' model (section 0), and there is no NFL validation of score-driven (GAS) models.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: The JRSS-A 2015 paper is a parameter-driven state-space model fit by importance sampling (Crossref abstract), not a score-driven/GAS model. The score-driven work is a later, separate Koopman-Lit paper, not cited or verified here. The label is carried over wrongly from FIX_AND_ADD/F08.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: nflverse/nflfastR supplies the neutral-situation definitions (win probability 20-80%, clock running, no spikes/kneels), per Sharp.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: The local nflfastR clone contains no neutral-situation definition; it only ships wp, qb_spike and qb_kneel columns. The cited Sharp page defines neutral as 'quarters 1 to 3 inside 14 points, excluding the final two minutes of the half', not WP 20-80% with the clock running. The definition is misattributed and misquoted.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Baker & McHale's structure uses separate TD and FG hazards.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: The abstract only mentions 'hazards of scoring' driven by team stats and/or the spread and over/under. The TD/FG split cannot be verified from what was read.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Moskowitz: over/under contracts specifically show about half of the open-to-close move reversed, and their returns fail to overcome costs.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: The -0.50 reversal coefficient comes from the pooled Table II regression across all contract types and sports, not an over/under-specific estimate. The transaction-cost statement covers momentum and value strategies in general. The over/under momentum strategy alone makes 17.12% a year gross (t=2.86). The direction is right but the claim is over-scoped.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Archived forecasts via Open-Meteo: Historical Forecast API from ~2022, Previous Runs API from January 2024.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: This is incomplete in a way that matters for the design. (1) The Historical Forecast API stitches the first few hours of each model run, so it gives very short-lead forecasts, close to realized weather, not what was knowable days before a bet. Using it for bets placed earlier brings back look-ahead. (2) The Previous Runs API gives fixed 1-7 day lead offsets and has GFS from March 2021 (JMA from 2018), so more usable history exists than the report says.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Total residual SD rises with the line (13.07 below 40 -> 13.6-13.8 at 48+), which justifies scaling SD with μ.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: The pattern is not monotone: 40-44 has SD 12.92, below the under-40 bucket's 13.07. The whole range is about 0.8 points on 5 buckets, so it is weak support for a μ-dependent SD term.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Red-zone TD rate is noise at the team-season level.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Its split-half r is 0.04, yet first-8 red-zone rate predicts rest-of-season points at r=0.18, better than plays (0.10), PROE (0.12) or the pace proxy (0.11). Near-zero split-half together with non-zero predictive r points to a construction artifact (per-play definition, per-game averaging of rates), not settled noise. 'Noise' is premature until it is re-measured per trip.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Expected gains over the market are likely under 0.2 RMSE; edges smaller than 1 point.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: No source or calculation supports either number. They are opinion.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Paul-Weinbach replication: lines 5+ points above the season mean went under 53.3%.
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: The number reproduces, but the season mean is taken over all of that season's lines, including games not yet played. As defined it is not a tradeable rule. It is fine as a descriptive check only.

recommendations_to_drop_or_change: Rec B2 (residual target = actual team points minus market-implied team total 'at decision time'): historical decision-time lines don't exist before the quote tape. game_lines holds near-close lines for all eras and opens only from 2020 (n≈1356). Training on closing-line residuals and then serving against an earlier line is a train/serve mismatch and effectively look-ahead. Train on the line actually available at the decision timestamp (open 2020+ or snapshots), accept the much smaller sample, and never grade CLV against the same close used as the training anchor.

Rec B1+B4 (one model, independent per-team PMFs convolved): zero linear residual correlation does not validate the joint PMF. If margin is also derived from two independent team PMFs, it will lose key-number mass (F17/Moyer: the independent model gets about half of P(margin=3)). Keep shared means μ_home and μ_away, but take the margin distribution from the existing key-number-tilted margin-distribution.js (or tilt a joint PMF on both margin and total), not from differencing independent team PMFs.
Rec B4 'scale SD with μ': drop, or use one shrunk linear term chosen walk-forward. The measured heteroscedasticity is under 1 point and not monotone.

Rec B5 weather: do not use the Open-Meteo Historical Forecast API (short-lead stitched runs) for bets placed days out. Use the Previous Runs API at the lead time that matches the bet (GFS back to March 2021), and pre-register a single wind test to avoid multiplicity. The 56.6% realized-wind result came from one bucket among many (4 wind buckets, 8 relative-line buckets) and must not be treated as a prior edge.

Rec B3 league scoring environment: compute it only from weeks and seasons strictly before the decision, never season-level means (the report's own replication used a same-season mean). Raw red-zone rates should not be dropped as 'noise' until re-measured per trip.

Rec B2 '30-60 features': with about 270 games a season, even fewer when decision-time lines are required, and two correlated rows per game, start from a small pre-registered feature set (about 10-15: opponent-adjusted offense/defense EPA/play and PPD, QB availability, forecast wind, rest). Choose λ by nested walk-forward that uses only prior seasons, and log every feature trial in the F06 registry. Otherwise ridge plus feature search will overfit.

Rec C nflfastR: borrow the column semantics (wp, qb_spike, qb_kneel, drive fields), but source the neutral-situation definition explicitly (for example Sharp's 'Q1-3 within 14 points excluding final two minutes of the half'), not attributed to nflfastR.
Rename the Koopman & Lit 2015 reference as a parameter-driven state-space model. Don't describe it as score-driven/GAS.
corrected_summary:
What survives verification:

(1) Literature. The NFL totals anomalies were real in older samples and have faded:
- Paul & Weinbach 2002 (1979-2000): unders on totals 5-7 points above the mean beat a fair bet.
- Kelly & Chen: unders on totals of 47.5 or more won 59.7% in 2001-09 (95-141, p=0.014) and lost in 2010-18 (47.1%). They attribute this to a change in sportsbook pricing.
- Borghesi 2008 (1984-2004): heat, wind and rain are under-priced, and a weather strategy beat 52.38% out of sample (abstract only).
- Kain & Logan (J. Sports Econ. 15(1), 2004-2010 data): the over/under is a poor predictor of total points while the spread is accurate (abstract).
- Moskowitz (JF 76(6), 2021): over/under returns are uncorrelated with spread returns and show the same open-to-close momentum. The roughly half reversal and the failure to overcome costs are pooled results across contract types, not totals-specific.
- Baker & McHale (IJF 2013) is an NFL point-process scoring-hazard model that about matches the market (abstract; the TD/FG split is unverified).
- Koopman & Lit 2015 is a soccer, parameter-driven state-space model, not score-driven. No NFL validation of dynamic bivariate Poisson was found.

(2) Gridiron data, reproduced exactly from the report's scripts:
- Closing totals are calibrated (slope 0.99 since 2020, RMSE 13.12) but explain about 8% of variance versus about 20% for spreads.
- Open-to-close total moves are not mispriced (slope 1.14 ± 0.16).
- The high-total under rule is 53.3% (n=383), not significant, and the rule used a same-season mean.
- Realized wind of 15+ mph: unders won 56.6% (n=617, z=2.07). This uses game-time wind, so it is look-ahead, and it is one test among many. It is only a hypothesis.
- Given the market-implied team totals, home and away residuals are nearly uncorrelated (0.00-0.035). Total residual SD is about 13 and only weakly, non-monotonically related to the line, with mild right skew. Totals key numbers are weak (51 is the most common at 3.85%).
- Team-season reliability (2016-25, n=320): offense EPA/play and PPD split-half about 0.6, predictive about 0.5. Defense is noisier (0.32). Pace and PROE are stable but weakly predictive.
- The red-zone TD rate is stored per play (confirmed in nfl-features.js). Split-half is about 0, yet it predicts rest-of-season points at r=0.18, so re-measure it per trip before calling it noise.

(3) Design that survives:
- Shared offense/defense ratings produce μ_home and μ_away, so spread and total are coherent.
- Take the margin distribution from the existing key-number-tilted margin PMF, not from differencing independent team PMFs. The total can come from convolving the team PMFs (pushes priced on integer totals).
- Use a ridge residual on the market line that was actually available at decision time. Historically that means open lines from 2020 or quote snapshots, not the close, so the sample is small.
- Keep a small pre-registered feature set, pick λ by nested walk-forward using prior seasons only, and log every trial in F06.
- Compute league scoring environment strictly from prior data.
- Test weather only with Open-Meteo Previous Runs forecasts at the matching lead time (GFS from March 2021). The Historical Forecast API's short-lead stitched data would leak.
- Gate the bet on continuous out-of-sample totals CLV against the true close from the quote tape.

(4) Code: penaltyblog (MIT, active; date < current date Backtest lookback, Dixon-Coles/bivariate Poisson) as a reference. nflfastR (MIT) for column semantics only. footBayes (GPL-2, needs Stan) as design reference only. Write ridge, PMF and convolution in-house in JS.

(5) Unsupported numbers to ignore: 'gains under 0.2 RMSE' and 'edges under 1 point' are opinion.
